effect_size.excerpt: When examining noninvasive cases only, no significant association was found in either men or women; for fruit and vegetable intake, HR = 1.24 (95% CI: 0.93, 1.64; P -trend = 0.11) in men and HR = 0.91 (95% CI: 0.51, 1.61; P -trend = 0.72) in women, and the P -interaction between sexes = 0.37 (data not shown).

confidence_interval.excerpt: In women, a dietary pattern characterized by the high intakes of fruit and milk was inversely associated with bladder cancer risk in the basic model [HR = 0.57 (95% CI: 0.34, 0.94); P -trend = 0.03]; however, the risk estimates were attenuated and not significant in the risk factor-adjusted model [HR = 0.75 (95% CI: 0.45, 1.25); P -trend = 0.30].

design.excerpt: The MEC Study is a longitudinal study designed to investigate the associations of dietary, lifestyle, and genetic factors with the incidence of cancer
design.location: Participants and Methods, Study population, paragraph 1

timing.excerpt: In a prospective analysis of 185,885 older adults participating in the Multiethnic Cohort Study, we examined whether the consumption of fruits and vegetables, or of nutrients concentrated in fruits and vegetables, was associated with bladder cancer risk.

continent.excerpt: by mailing a self-administered, 26-page questionnaire to men and women aged 45–75 y who were residing in Hawaii and California.
continent.location: Participants and Methods, Study population, paragraph 1

ethnicity.excerpt: 5 main ethnic groups (African Americans, Japanese Americans, Latinos, Native Hawaiians, and whites)
ethnicity.location: Participants and Methods, Study population, paragraph 1

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary intake was measured at baseline by using a quantitative FFQ (QFFQ) that assessed the frequency and quantity of food items consumed during the preceding year
exposure_measurement.location: Participants and Methods, Dietary assessment, paragraph 1
